description: Regression definition for the pydebug RISC-V Debug verification suite.
This file declares the TIERS and the FEATURE list. It deliberately does NOT
list individual test names: those are carried by pytest markers on the tests
themselves, so a test cannot silently fall out of the regression by someone
forgetting to update a manifest. tests/test_regression_integrity.py enforces
the policy below against the live test session.
To add a test to the regression: mark it @pytest.mark.feature('<feature id>').
That alone puts it in the static tier. Add @pytest.mark.smoke to also make it

smoke.description: One basic test per feature. The fast gate.
smoke.goal: Prove every feature is minimally alive. Catches gross breakage in seconds, with no simulator.
policy: Every feature with implemented tests MUST have at least one smoke test.
Smoke tests must be the BASIC, happy-path case for their feature -- not a corner case.
Smoke must stay fast: mock-backed only, no simulator, no hardware.

static.goal: Run the complete suite and close functional coverage. This is the tier that must give maximum architectural coverage whenever it runs.
policy: Contains every test, including all smoke tests.
Includes the coverage-closure check: the functional coverage model must report every non-excluded bin hit.
Includes the invariant check: no architectural violation across the whole trace.
Excluded coverage bins must carry a spec-cited reason and are reported separately -- never counted as covered.

status_values.planned: Declared, tests not written yet. Exempt from the must-have-tests rule.
status_values.partial: Some tests exist; the feature is not fully covered yet.
status_values.complete: Every planned TC-ID for this feature has a test.
status_values.framework: Not a spec feature - infrastructure that still needs regression cover.

description: Simulator-backed regressions are NOT part of the pytest tiers above: they need
Questa and a built DUT, and run via the per-SoC Makefiles. Listed here so the
regression definition is complete in one place.

targets.note: hasresethaltreq=0 on CVA6 (dm_csrs.sv:235) — TC-HOR-002..005 report N/A on this DUT; only TC-HOR-001 (the gate) and TC-HOR-005 (ungated negative test) exercise real DUT behaviour here.

TC-HS-002's nonexistent-hart assertion is only rigorous against a golden-model-backed transport (real num_harts is not otherwise discoverable); on real DUTs this step is informational only, per hart_selection_sequence.py.
